text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government on Friday launched its economic reforms package announcing substantial cuts in tariffs, personal and corporate taxes, general sales tax and abolished regulatory duty. But some economists say the package is likely to widen budget deficit.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has ordered the authorities to hold an inquiry into the wheat flour shortage and find out its causes.
- Businessmen and industrialists expect a price cut of about five to 10 percent following substantial decline in import and local tariffs announced by the government on Friday.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has said the government will consult traders and businessmen to work out a system for imposing three percent general sales tax at the retail level from July 1.
- The economic package will reduce the upfront investment cost of projects by 25 to 30 percent.
- The International Monetary Fund has endorsed the economic reforms programme, Sartaj Aziz said.
- Foreign secretaries level talks between India and Pakistan have started in New Delhi on an optimistic note.
- The Senate (upper house) was assured by the government that the wheat crises will be over within a couple of days as ships were unloading wheat at Karachi port.
